data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The stall at rank 23 for <3,3,3> is best explained by a rationality-and-symmetry obstruction: any rank-22 decomposition over a characteristic-0 field must place coefficient-matrix entries in a number-field extension of degree \u2265 2, and no such decomposition exists over Q. This predicts (a) exhaustive bounded-denominator rational search finds no rank-22 solution, (b) floating-point ALS searches approach but never certify rank 22, and (c) a rank-22 solution may exist modulo some small prime p without lifting to characteristic 0.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A rank-22 decomposition with all coefficient matrices having rational entries is found and sandbox-verified.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A rank-22 decomposition over a quadratic number field is found and sandbox-verified, contradicting the impossibility claim for degree-2 extensions.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"An exhaustive search over rational coefficient matrices with bounded denominators (e.g., |entries| \u2264 B for B up to 10^4) finds a rank-22 solution, showing the obstruction is not rationality but search-depth.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A structural lemma proving that the orbit-stabilizer argument is vacuous (e.g., because rank-1 terms need not lie in distinct symmetry orbits) is demonstrated.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The symmetry group of <3,3,3> (factor permutations plus inner automorphisms from GL_3^3) acts on the set of rank-r decompositions. For rank 23, Laderman's construction has a residual symmetry (order-3 cyclic) that is compatible with rational coefficients. Reducing to 22 terms forces the orbit structure to break this cyclic symmetry: the 22 rank-1 terms cannot be partitioned into orbits whose sizes sum to 22 while preserving the trilinear identity over Q. The only escape is to allow coefficients in a quadratic or higher extension where the orbit-stabilizer constraints relax, but the polynomial identity conditions (729 integer comparisons) then require algebraic-integer cancellations that are provably impossible for degree-2 extensions because the Galois conjugate of any valid decomposition would give a second distinct valid decomposition, and the tensor's known degeneracy structure forbids two conjugate decompositions from both being rank-minimal.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
